BioNTech cuts sales forecast on slumping demand for COVID-19 vaccine
snippet: Lower vaccine demand across every market and more acute pressures in Germany led BioNTech to lower the midpoint of its sales outlook by almost 20%.

title: Supernus, Indivior merger expected to result in ‘natural redundancies’
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: As portfolio erodes, BMS stands to gain a lot from rumored AstraZeneca merger
snippet: While both drugmakers face looming patent cliffs, analysts say joining forces could help Bristol Myers Squibb replenish its eroding portfolio—while the strategic case for AstraZeneca seems to be more mixed.

title: Pfizer cuts $2.5B more across R&D, manufacturing in ongoing restructure
snippet: The additional cuts, which will primarily occur between 2027 and 2029, will cost some $6 billion as the pharma tries to ride out a post-COVID headache while facing stiff patent headwinds for major products like the blood thinner Eliquis.

title: Latigo, BlossomHill detail IPO plans for pain and cancer push
snippet: Latigo Biotherapeutics is looking to raise up to $285.2 million for a non-opioid analgesic, while BlossomHill Therapeutics is eyeing up to $129.1 million in proceeds for its oncology pipeline.

title: Pathos inks back-to-back cancer contracts with AstraZeneca, China’s Alphamab
snippet: Pathos AI could pay more than $2 billion to a Jiangsu Alphamab Biopharmaceuticals subsidiary for a late-stage bispecific antibody-drug conjugate for breast cancer, while the financial details of the AstraZeneca agreement were not disclosed.

title: Vertex unfazed by competitive IgAN space as FDA verdict looms
snippet: Positive two-year follow-up data for Otsuka Pharmaceuticals’ IgA nephropathy drug Voyxact could support the FDA’s ongoing review of Vertex Pharmaceuticals’ povetacicept, CEO Reshma Kewalramani said on the company’s second quarter earnings call.

title: Supernus and Indivior merge to create CNS mega-company with 11 approved drugs
snippet: Supernus Pharmaceuticals and Indivior Pharmaceuticals are outlining a combined expected $2.2 billion in annual revenue, plus $125 million in cost savings that will include “natural redundancies.”

title: BioNTech picks Sobi CEO Oelkers to lead as founders plot new mRNA biotech
snippet: BioNTech’s leadership transition was announced earlier this year, with CEO Ugur Sahin and CMO Özlem Türeci leaving to start a new mRNA company. Guido Oelkers of Swedish Orphan Biovitrum AB will take over as CEO in early 2027.

title: Novo’s late-stage IL-6 stumble shakes inflammation space
snippet: Novo Nordisk was banking on the inflammatory benefits of its investigational therapy ziltivekimab to improve cardiovascular outcomes. Last week’s Phase 3 failure dashed not just the Danish pharma’s hopes but that of other drugmakers working on the same pathway.

title: ‘Unlikely’ AstraZeneca-BMS mega-merger would be largest pharma deal ever
snippet: If AstraZeneca and Bristol Myers Squibb were to successfully become one company, analysts say it could reset the current deal environment, which has picked up greatly in the first half of the year.

title: Amgen hit with cybersecurity breach, patient data affected
snippet: The hack is unlikely to affect Amgen’s financial reporting and other operations, nor does the pharma expect its ability to meet patient needs will be compromised.

title: Biologics push CMOs/CDMOs to expand sterile fill-finish and prefilled syringe capacity
snippet: As biologics, biosimilars and GLP-1s drive demand for sterile drug products, CMOs and CDMOs are investing in fill-finish, lyophilization, inspection and packaging capacity to keep pace with a dynamic injectable market.

title: Biotech leaders call for streamlining of INDs as FDA’s Trialblazer rolls out
snippet: The FDA’s new investigational new drug pilot program—one part of HHS’s broader clinical trial modernization initiatives—has lofty goals to expedite first-in-human trials of novel drugs, but experts say it won’t tip the scales much on its own.

title: 5 companies advancing ATTR assets in the wake of Wainua’s fail
snippet: The Phase 3 failure of AstraZeneca and Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ antisense therapy in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy last month left the space reeling—and readjusting. BioSpace looks at five contenders and where they currently stand.

title: Capricor CEO won’t rule out legal action against FDA after negative adcomm
snippet: After an FDA advisory committee voted 9-3 on Wednesday against recommending Capricor Therapeutics’ Duchenne muscular dystrophy cardiomyopathy drug for approval, stakeholders allege an “ulterior motive” and “biased intentions.”

title: Lilly and Resilience invest $750M in diabetes and obesity drug device supply
snippet: The investment will expand Resilience’s U.S. capacity to make the KwikPen device Eli Lilly uses to deliver its injectable diabetes and obesity medicines.

title: AbbVie shares pressured as Q2 I&I beat falls below investor expectations
snippet: AbbVie investors’ sky-high expectations led to a 4% share decline on Friday as the company reported more modest consensus beats than expected.

title: Novo's IL-6 inhibitor fails in cardiovascular Phase 3, plunging shares more than 9%
snippet: Novo Nordisk's IL-6 inhibitor ziltivekimab failed to reduce the risk of cardiovascular events in the late-stage trial, dashing hopes for an edge in the hyper-competitive cardiometabolic space.

title: Moderna maintains 10% growth target despite Phase 3 norovirus miss
snippet: Moderna’s norovirus vaccine failed in a Phase 3 trial, but the company still has faith in an ambitious revenue growth target thanks to ex-U.S. vaccine sales and a unanimous FDA adcomm win for mFLUSIVA.

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?

title: Lilly just bought renowned regulator Peter Marks a pipeline to play with
snippet: FDA veteran Peter Marks will now shape the future of Eli Lilly’s vaccines work after the buys of Curevo, LimmaTech Biologics and Vaccine Company for up to $3.8 billion total.
